title: Each decoupling cap must be placed at its owner IC power pad
rule: Every bypass/decoupling capacitor must be placed within the courtyard envelope of its owner IC (or immediately adjacent, outside but touching the courtyard edge), on the same side of the board. The net shared between cap and IC must match verify_passives() expectations.
scope: All C* refs where the net is a power rail (+3V3, +5VSB, VBUS, VCC) and the cap is <=1 uF. Ownership derived by derive_passive_spec() / auto_cluster() from strongest net coupling to an IC power pin.
rationale: Decoupling caps must be close to their IC's power pins to suppress switching noise; a cap parked far away has high inductance and provides no benefit. cec_pcb.auto_cluster() places each cap just outside the owner IC courtyard edge nearest the power pad.
check_method: For each (cap, owner IC) pair from derive_passive_spec: compute Euclidean distance between cap centroid and nearest power pad of owner IC. Fail if distance > (IC_courtyard_half_diagonal + cap_courtyard_half_diagonal + 1.5 mm clearance).
source: CLAUDE.md done-items: 'PASSIVE ENGINE = every decoupling/RC/pull-up/ESD passive placed in its OWNER IC cluster from a netlist-verified ownership spec (PASSIVE_SPEC: part->IC->expected net), re-checked at build by verify_passives() (25/25 verified)'

title: Sense IC (INA238/INA240/INA181) must be adjacent to its shunt inner edge
rule: Each INA238, INA240, or INA181 sense IC must be placed such that its IN+ and IN- pads (the Kelvin sense inputs) are within 3 mm of the inner sense-tap edge of its associated shunt resistor. No other components may be interposed between the shunt inner edge and the INA sense pins.
scope: All U* refs with footprint containing INA238, INA240, or INA181. For each, find the shunt RS* that shares the *_HI/*_LO nets. Inner shunt edge = pad 1 for _HI net (upper at rot270), pad 2 for _LO net (lower at rot270).
rationale: Kelvin four-wire sensing requires the voltage taps to originate at the shunt inner pad edges, not the outer force-current pads. A long trace from shunt to INA picks up IR drop from supply/return current. CLAUDE.md action item -2 explicitly calls this out as a hard constraint that the auto-placer must enforce.
check_method: For each (INA_ref, shunt_ref) pair sharing *_HI/*_LO nets: compute distance between INA IN+/IN- pad global positions and shunt inner-edge pad global positions. Fail if > 3 mm.
existing_checker: cec_score.kelvin_ok (gates on routed connectivity, not placement distance)
source: CLAUDE.md action item -2: '(2) sense-IC-adjacent-to-shunt as a hard constraint (Kelvin)'; cec_pcb.py auto_cluster docstring; gen-eps-condensed.py: INA238 at (Xc+0.5, 17.5) with shunt at (Xc+6.8, 17.5)

title: Kelvin sense traces must route on F.Cu only, no layer changes
rule: The *_HI and *_LO Kelvin sense net traces from shunt inner pads to INA sense inputs must be routed entirely on F.Cu (the top copper layer), with zero vias between shunt pad and INA input pin. They must run over the In1 GND plane for controlled impedance return.
scope: All nets matching *_HI or *_LO suffixes (Kelvin pairs as derived by cec_score._derive_pairs). Trace segment layer must be F.Cu for all segments from shunt pad to INA pin.
rationale: A via in a Kelvin sense path adds contact resistance and inductance. The sense path must be a low-resistance, low-inductance direct copper path. Routing over the GND plane (In1) gives a short, well-defined return.
check_method: For each Kelvin net, inspect all routed track segments. If any segment is not on F.Cu, or if any via exists on the net between shunt pad and INA pad, fail.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items routing plan: 'Kelvin pairs Cmts.User... sense off the INNER shunt edges, RC filter at the INA'; gen-eps-condensed.py: 'Kelvin taps confirmed non-crossing'; 12VHPWR routing plan: 'Kelvin pair 0.2-0.25mm tight matched pair over the In1 GND plane, sense off the INNER shunt edges'

title: Kelvin taps must originate from inner shunt pad edges, not outer
rule: The *_HI Kelvin tap must connect to pad 1 of its shunt (the pad facing the sense IC / inner edge at rot270), and *_LO must connect to pad 2 (the lower inner edge). The trace must leave from the inner-facing edge of the pad, not the outer force-current edge.
scope: All RS* shunt footprints with rot270 orientation on EPS/PCIe boards. Pad 1 = _HI (upper/inner), pad 2 = _LO (lower/inner).
rationale: The entire point of Kelvin (four-wire) sensing is to pick up the voltage across the shunt body at the exact points where current enters and exits, not including the via/pad contact resistance. Tapping the outer pad edge measures contact resistance in addition to the shunt.
check_method: Inspect shunt rotation: must be rot270 on EPS/PCIe. Confirm pad 1 net is *_HI and pad 2 net is *_LO in the netlist. Verify no net assignment inversion.
source: gen-eps-condensed.py: 'P[f"RS{c}"] = (Xc + 6.8, 17.5, 270)' and 'Kelvin route data: taps from inner shunt edge at (rsx, 15.9) and (rsx, 19.1)'; CLAUDE.md done-items: 'shunt rot 90->270 so HI is the upper terminal'

title: Kelvin _HI and _LO traces must be length-matched within 0.5 mm
rule: For each Kelvin pair (*_HI / *_LO), the total routed copper length from shunt pad to INA sense pin must be matched within 0.5 mm between the two members of the pair.
scope: All (*_HI, *_LO) net pairs as derived by cec_score._derive_pairs. Measure track length on F.Cu only.
rationale: A length mismatch in the Kelvin pair creates a net-resistance asymmetry between IN+ and IN- paths, introducing a small differential offset voltage. For the near-DC current sense application this is a second-order error, but it should be minimized to keep the Kelvin geometry clean.
check_method: Sum F.Cu track lengths for each member of a Kelvin pair. Compute |L_HI - L_LO|. Fail if > 0.5 mm.
existing_checker: cec_score (HPWL / track length metrics available, not yet per-pair length)
source: CLAUDE.md done-items 12VHPWR: 'length-match the straight run in the GUI if the inner/outer spread matters'; spec §6.8 Kelvin sensing

title: INA240 RC anti-alias filter (RFH/RFL + CF) must be placed at INA input pins
rule: For each INA240 on the 12VHPWR Standard board, the matched 10-ohm series filter resistors (RFH_n, RFL_n) and 470 nF differential cap (CF_n) must be placed within 2 mm of the INA240 IN+/IN- pads. RFH and RFL must be equidistant from the INA to maintain CMRR.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board only. Parts: RFH1-6 / RFL1-6 (10 ohm, 0.1%) and CF1-6 (470 nF). Owner ICs: INA240 instances U_pin1 through U_pin6 (or equivalent refs).
rationale: The RC filter sets fc ~16.9 kHz (-3 dB) to pass 10 kHz GPU transients at -1.3 dB while attenuating HF. The TI application note caps Rf at 10 ohm to limit gain/CMRR degradation. If RFH/RFL are not matched in position relative to the INA, there is a CMRR imbalance. Placement at the INA pins keeps the filtered sense path short.
check_method: For each INA240 instance, find its RFH_n and RFL_n resistors. Measure distance from RFH_n/RFL_n to INA IN+ and IN- pads respectively. Fail if > 2 mm. Verify RFH_n and RFL_n are equidistant from their respective INA pads within 0.3 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md spec v3.4 additions: '(a) a per-channel INA240 input anti-alias/transient RC filter — matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input (RFH/RFL1-6) + a 470 nF differential cap (CF1-6), fc = 1/(2*pi*2*Rf*Cdiff) ~= 16.9 kHz... Rf held at 10 ohm + matched (TI's INA240 ceiling)'

title: Six INA240 must be in 6 symmetric columns at equal pitch
rule: The six INA240 per-pin sense ICs on the 12VHPWR Standard board must be arranged in 6 columns of equal spacing (nominal 6 mm pitch). Each column must be vertically aligned with its shunt resistor and the corresponding J3/J4 connector pin pair. Column pitch must be uniform: max deviation between adjacent column X-positions <= 0.1 mm.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. INA240 refs and their paired shunts (RS1-RS6) plus J3/J4 power pin columns.
rationale: Each 12V pin of the 12V-2x6 connector carries independent current. The fan-out layout assigns one column per pin, enabling equal-length Kelvin taps and equal-length high-current traces from J3 through shunt to J4. Asymmetric columns would create length-mismatched sense paths and unequal thermal loading.
check_method: Extract X-positions of INA240 instances. Sort. Compute differences between adjacent X values. Fail if max(differences) - min(differences) > 0.2 mm (non-uniform pitch).
source: gen-hpwr-route-status.py: 'LANE_X = [116.875+6*k for k in range(6)]'; CLAUDE.md: 'six +12V lanes splay symmetrically to a ~6mm SENSE pitch so each lane gets its OWN column'

title: 12VHPWR J3 (in) must be at top edge, J4 (out) at bottom edge, shunts between
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard board: J3 (PSU input) must be placed at the top board edge (min Y, mouth facing up/out), J4 (GPU output) at the bottom edge (max Y, mouth facing down/out). All shunt resistors RS1-RS6 must have Y-coordinates strictly between J3 connector pad Y-positions and J4 connector pad Y-positions.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. J3, J4, RS1-RS6.
rationale: 12V current flows top-to-bottom: PSU cable enters J3 at top, flows down through each shunt (measurement point), and exits J4 to GPU. This straight vertical current path minimizes inductance, ensures each shunt is in the single current path, and allows the two outer copper layers to carry 12V vertically in parallel for low resistance.
check_method: Verify J3 Y-centroid < J4 Y-centroid. Verify all RS* Y-centroids satisfy J3_Y < RS_Y < J4_Y.
source: gen-hpwr-route-status.py: 'J3 at y=62.67, J4 at y=131.83'; CLAUDE.md: '12V power path TOP->BOTTOM down the centre-left (J3 MALE header IN top-centre... J4 captive-pigtail OUT bottom-centre)'

title: Control ICs and decoupling caps must not be placed in the 12V high-current corridor
rule: The 6-column 12V high-current corridor (bounding box from leftmost J3 +12V pin column to rightmost, extended top-to-bottom between J3 and J4) must be free of all non-power-path components: no ESP32, CAN transceiver, LDO, or signal-path passives inside this corridor.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. Corridor: X from left-column J3 pin minus 1 mm to right-column J3 pin plus 1 mm, Y from J3 pad top to J4 pad bottom. Exclude: RS1-RS6, INA240 instances, RFH/RFL, CF caps.
rationale: The high-current corridor carries up to ~40A aggregate (6 pins x ~6.7A each). Logic components inside the corridor would (a) be subjected to magnetic field from the current loops, (b) interfere with copper pour routing, (c) create thermal coupling from high-I2R heating. Action item -2 explicitly calls out corridor keepout as a hard constraint.
check_method: Define corridor_bbox from J3/J4 pin positions. For each non-power-path component, check if its courtyard_bbox overlaps corridor_bbox. Fail on any overlap.
source: CLAUDE.md action item -2: '(1) high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation'; gen-hpwr-route-status.py: corridor implicitly defined by LANE_X array

title: REF3030 must be adjacent to ESP32 ADC pin, VREF trace < 10 mm
rule: U4 (REF3030, 3.0V reference) on the 12VHPWR Standard board must be placed within 5 mm of the ESP32-S3-MINI-1 ADC1 IO8 pin pad. The VREF net trace from REF3030 OUT to ESP32 IO8 must be <= 10 mm total length.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board only. U4 = REF3030, U1 = ESP32-S3-MINI-1, net VREF.
rationale: REF3030 is the ratiometric reference measured by the ESP32 ADC (firmware divides all INA240 outputs by the REF3030 reading to cancel ADC gain/offset drift). The VREF trace must be short and routed away from noisy 12V traces to avoid injecting noise into the reference measurement. REF3030 OUT = 3.0V, must remain within ESP32 ADC input range (< 3.3V absolute max).
check_method: Compute distance between U4 centroid and U1 IO8 pad global position. Fail if > 5 mm. If tracks are routed, sum VREF track length; fail if > 10 mm.
source: gen-hpwr-route-status.py: 'REF3030 U4+bypass planned at (149.8, 98.0) near ESP'; CLAUDE.md v3.8: 'REF3030 (3.0V, SOT-23, measured on ESP ADC1 IO8 for ratiometric correction)'

title: 12VHPWR Standard must use REF3030 (3.0V), not REF3033 (3.3V)
rule: The BOM value for U4 on the 12VHPWR Standard board must be REF3030 (VOUT = 3.0V, LCSC C38423). REF3033 (3.3V) is strictly forbidden: it would over-range the ESP32 ADC (absolute max ~3.6V, but 3.3V = rail = no headroom). The Standard module's reference feeds the ADC; the Pro module's REF3033 feeds the LTC2358-18 reference input — entirely different use.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board only. U4.
rationale: REF3030 = 3.0V output, safely within the 3.3V ADC range for ratiometric measurement. REF3033 = 3.3V would saturate the ESP32 ADC and potentially damage the input. The two parts are NOT interchangeable between Standard and Pro despite similar names.
check_method: Read U4 BOM Value field. Fail if not 'REF3030' or LCSC is not C38423.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.8: 'Standard REF3030=3.0V is MEASURED by the ADC (must sit in the ADC range); the Pro's REF3033=3.3V feeds the LTC2358 ref (different use)'

title: Rail divider R5 must tap SENSEP6_HI (the INA240 pin closest to the ESP)
rule: The 47k/10k rail voltage divider input resistor R5 on 12VHPWR Standard must connect to net SENSEP6_HI (or equivalent: the +12V sense net of the INA240 column closest to the ESP32). It must NOT tap SENSEP1_HI or any other column.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. R5 (47k), net SENSEP6_HI -> VRAIL_DIV -> R6 (10k) -> GND.
rationale: All 6 SENSEP*_HI nets are electrically identical (+12V rail). Tapping the closest column to the ESP minimizes the VRAIL_DIV trace length, reducing noise pickup and routing congestion. Moving the tap to any other column is legal but wastes routing resources.
check_method: From netlist: verify R5 pin 1 is on SENSEP6_HI (or the equivalent numerically-highest SENSEP net). Warn if on any lower-numbered SENSEP net.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'moved the 47k/10k rail-divider input R5.1 from SENSEP1_HI -> SENSEP6_HI (pin-6 HI, closest to the ESP) -- electrically identical... just shorter routing'

title: VRAIL_DIV ADC smoothing cap C24 must be placed at the divider node
rule: C24 (1 nF C0G, Murata GRM1555C1H102JA01D / LCSC C76947) must be placed at the VRAIL_DIV node, within 1 mm of the junction of R5 and R6 (the center node of the 47k/10k divider). VRAIL_DIV net connects C24.1, R5.2, R6.1, and ESP32 IO7 ADC input.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board only. C24, R5, R6, net VRAIL_DIV.
rationale: C24 filters the VRAIL_DIV node against the ESP32 SAR S&H transient and HF noise, with fc ~19 kHz using the 47k||10k source (matching the ~16.9 kHz INA channels). Placement at the node minimizes the capacitance from series trace inductance.
check_method: Verify C24 net is VRAIL_DIV. Compute distance from C24 centroid to R5-R6 junction pad. Fail if > 1.5 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'VRAIL_DIV ADC cap DONE 2026-06-06 -- added C24 = 1nF C0G (Murata GRM1555C1H102JA01D / C76947) VRAIL_DIV->GND, fc~19kHz with the 47k||10k source... spliced near R6 at (107.95,270.51)'

title: NTC thermistor TH1 must be placed adjacent to the shunt row (board/shunt temp)
rule: TH1 (Murata NCP15XH103F03RC / LCSC C77131) on boards with NTC temperature monitoring must be placed within 3 mm of the nearest shunt resistor pad, on the same side of the board. TH1 is the board/shunt temperature sensor.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board: TH1 adjacent to J3 +12V pins / shunt row. gen-hpwr-route-status.py shows planned position at (150.5, 77.5).
rationale: TH1 reads shunt/board temperature for INA240 gain-drift compensation and overheat detection. If it is remote from the shunts, it reads ambient instead of shunt temp, providing useless data for shunt-TCR correction.
check_method: Find TH1 centroid. Find nearest RS* shunt pad. Fail if distance > 3 mm.
source: gen-hpwr-route-status.py: TH1 at (150.5, 77.5) annotated 'NTC on the 12V pour BY THE SHUNT ROW'; CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'TH1 by the shunt row = board/shunt temp'

title: NTC thermistor TH2 must be in an ambient/cool corner, away from 12V section
rule: TH2 (ambient NTC) must be placed in a corner of the board that is thermally isolated from the 12V high-current corridor. Minimum separation: 10 mm from any shunt resistor and 5 mm from any high-current power trace. Must NOT be in or adjacent to the 12V corridor keepout zone.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board: TH2 at cool corner. gen-hpwr-route-status.py shows planned position at (118.0, 124.5).
rationale: TH2 is the ambient temperature reference. Its delta from TH1 gives dT-above-ambient for the shunt/board health calculation. If TH2 is heated by the 12V section it reads a falsely elevated ambient, making the dT measurement useless.
check_method: Compute distance from TH2 to nearest RS* shunt. Fail if < 10 mm. Compute distance from TH2 to 12V corridor keepout zone. Fail if < 5 mm.
source: gen-hpwr-route-status.py: TH2 at (118.0, 124.5) annotated 'NTC at a COOL CORNER (ambient ref, isolated from the 12V section)'; CLAUDE.md v3.7: 'TH2 ambient'

title: SK6812 level-shifter U6 must be placed adjacent to ESP32 LED_DATA GPIO
rule: U6 (SN74AHCT1G08, SOT-23-5, level-shifter for SK6812 chain) must be placed within 3 mm of ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 IO25 pad (the LED_DATA output). C14 (100 nF bypass for U6 VCC) must be within 1 mm of U6 VCC pin. R14 (330 ohm series into DL1.DIN) must be between U6 output and DL1.DIN, within 5 mm of U6.
scope: Hub Standard board only. U6, C14, R14, chain: U1.IO25 -> U6 -> R14 -> DL1.DIN.
rationale: The ESP32's 3.3V IO25 is below the SK6812 VIH (0.7*5V = 3.5V). Without the level shifter (or with it placed far away), the LED chain may receive marginal signals causing glitches or missed data. U6 as a non-inverting AHCT buffer (both inputs tied, VCC=5V) provides a clean 5V signal.
check_method: Compute distance from U6 centroid to U1 IO25 pad global position. Fail if > 3 mm. Compute distance from C14 to U6 VCC pad. Fail if > 1 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'SK6812 data level shift (2026-06-05): U6 (SN74AHCT1G08 single 2-input AND with both inputs tied = a non-inverting AHCT buffer; SOT-23-5, VCC=+5VSB, C14 100 nF)... chain U1.IO25->U6->R14->DL1.DIN'

title: DETECT ESD diode must be within 5 mm of RJ-45 pin 8 pad
rule: Each PESD5V0S1BA ESD diode (D2-D5 on Hub Standard; D1 on modules) must be placed within 5 mm of the RJ-45 jack pin 8 pad it protects, on F.Cu. Cathode must connect to the DETECT net; anode must connect to GND.
scope: Hub Standard: D2-D5, one per RJ-45 port J2-J5. Modules: D1, one per board. Footprint: SOD-323.
rationale: The DETECT pin 8 is an analog ADC input directly exposed to the cable. Hot-plug insertion ESD can reach the pin before the board is clamped. The ESD diode must be within a few mm of the pin 8 pad to clamp transients before they propagate to the MCU ADC input.
check_method: For each DETECT diode (matching PESD5V0S1BA value), find the nearest RJ-45 pin-8 pad. Fail if distance > 5 mm. Verify cathode net = DETECT_n, anode net = GND.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'LOCKED (v2.0): one low-capacitance ESD diode on the DETECT pin (pin 8 -> ESP32 ADC) on EVERY Hub and module, for hot-plug insertion ESD on the bare analog input'

title: CAN transceiver U2 must be adjacent to ESP32 CAN_TX/CAN_RX pads
rule: U2 (TJA1051T/3, SO-8) must be placed within 5 mm of the ESP32 CAN_TX and CAN_RX pads. The stub trace from ESP32 GPIO to TJA1051T/3 TXD/RXD must be < 10 mm total length.
scope: All boards with U2 TJA1051T/3 (Hub Standard, all modules). EPS/PCIe: CAN_TX/RX -> IO20/21 pads 26/27 on C6-MINI-1; 12VHPWR: S3-MINI-1 pinout.
rationale: A long stub between MCU and CAN transceiver creates signal reflections and can cause CAN errors, especially at the optional 1 Mbps rate. The transceiver should be close to the MCU so the differential CAN_H/CAN_L traces carry clean signals.
check_method: Compute distance from U2 centroid to ESP32 CAN_TX and CAN_RX pad global positions. Fail if > 5 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md routing pass: 'move U2 next to the ESP CAN pins (it's top-right, CAN_TX/RX cross the whole board)'; gen-eps-condensed.py routing plan

title: All through-board connectors must have their mating face directed toward the nearest board edge
rule: Every connector (RJ-45, USB-C, power, CAN) must be oriented so its mating interface faces outward toward the nearest board edge, enabling cable connection without the cable touching the board surface. Specifically: J_IN mouth faces top edge, J_OUT mouth faces bottom edge (EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR); J1 (RJ-45) mouth faces right edge; J5 (USB-C) mouth faces right edge.
scope: All boards. Connectors: J_IN*, J_OUT*, J1 (RJ-45), J5 (USB-C), J7 (NanoKVM).
rationale: If a connector's mating face is not oriented toward the board edge, cables cannot be plugged in without the cable overmold striking the board or other components. Rotational errors in connector placement are a fabrication defect.
check_method: For each connector, determine the mating-face direction from the footprint definition. Verify the vector from board centroid to connector centroid aligns with the mating-face outward direction within 15 degrees.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items: 'J_IN rot180 / J_OUT rot0 (mouth top/bottom)'; '(RJ-45) and J5 (USB-C) overhang the RIGHT edge'; gen-eps-condensed.py placement table

title: PSU-side connectors must overhang the board edge so bodies clear the plug overmold
rule: J_IN and J_OUT (PSU-side power connectors) on EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR boards must be placed with their solder pads on-board and their connector bodies/mouths partially overhanging the board edge. The THT solder pads must be within the board outline; the connector shroud/mouth may extend past Edge.Cuts.
scope: EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR boards. J_IN*, J_OUT*.
rationale: The Molex 87427-0802 and 45586-0005 connectors have a large shroud/mouth that extends beyond the THT pads. If the entire connector body is inside the board, the cable overmold would hit the PCB edge. Overhanging the body lets the cable plug in cleanly while keeping all electrical contacts on-board.
check_method: Verify at least one pad of J_IN/J_OUT is inside the board outline (not on Edge.Cuts or outside). Verify the connector courtyard extends past Edge.Cuts by at least 1 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items: 'PLUG connectors OVERHANG their edge so a cable seats without the board fouling the plug overmold while the solder pads stay on-board: J3 right-angle shroud/mouth (~9.5mm deep) overhangs the TOP edge ~3mm'

title: At least 3 M3 GND-tied mounting holes must be at board corners
rule: Every board must have at least 3 M3 mounting holes (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via footprint), all tied to GND net, placed at or near board corners (within 5 mm of corner). The holes must not overlap with connector courtyards.
scope: All boards. M3 mount refs: H1, H2, H3 (or equivalent). Footprint: cec-MountingHole:MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via.
rationale: M3 corner mounts provide mechanical chassis attachment and chassis grounding. Chassis grounding of the GND plane (via the mount screw to a grounded standoff) reduces common-mode noise. Three non-collinear mounts create a stable mechanical triangle. v3.2 locked M3 (up from M2.5).
check_method: Count mounting hole refs. Fail if < 3. For each mount, compute distance to nearest board corner. Fail if all mounts have corner distance > 5 mm. Verify each mount has a net assignment of GND.
source: CLAUDE.md: '3 M3 mounts (2 left strip, 1 bottom-right below the RJ-45)'; spec v3.2: 'M2.5->M3 corner mounts'

title: Hub Standard ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 PCB antenna keepout must be copper-free
rule: The ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 PCB antenna keepout area (as defined in the ESP32 hardware design guidelines, approximately 2 mm extension from the module edge on the antenna side) must have no copper fills, pours, or traces on any layer. The keepout must be maintained on F.Cu, B.Cu, In1.Cu, and In2.Cu.
scope: Hub Standard board only. U1 = ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8. Keepout area as defined by the footprint antenna-keepout graphic.
rationale: Copper in the antenna keepout zone detunes the onboard PCB antenna, degrading Wi-Fi/BT performance. Even if Wi-Fi is not used in the current firmware, the antenna keepout must be respected for future Wi-Fi use (CLAUDE.md: 'PCB-antenna keepout honored for future Wi-Fi').
check_method: Check for copper (tracks, fills, zones) within the ESP32 WROOM antenna keepout bounding box on any copper layer.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline: respect_antenna_keepout parameter; cec_pcb.courtyard_bbox drop_keepout=False for WROOM
source: CLAUDE.md: 'ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (16 MB flash + 8 MB PSRAM, PCB-antenna keepout honored for future Wi-Fi)'

title: ESP32-C6-MINI-1 antenna keepout may be dropped on wired-only sensor modules
rule: On EPS, PCIe, and 24-pin modules (wired-only, no Wi-Fi populated), the ESP32-C6-MINI-1 antenna keepout SHOULD be dropped (not enforced), allowing copper fills under the antenna lobe for tighter board density. The footprint courtyard should be trimmed to body-only (no antenna lobe keepout) via cec_pcb.courtyard_bbox(drop_keepout=True).
scope: EPS, PCIe-2port, PCIe-3port, 24-pin ATX boards. U1 = ESP32-C6-MINI-1.
rationale: Wired-only modules have no use for Wi-Fi/BT; enforcing the antenna keepout wastes board area. The placer respects the keepout by default for DRC-consistency; dropping it is a deliberate area optimization for boards confirmed as wired-only.
check_method: Advisory check: if board is classified wired-only AND any copper is present under the antenna lobe of ESP32-C6, verify this is intentional (check BOM for RF shield or Wi-Fi firmware flag absent).
existing_checker: cec_pcb.courtyard_bbox drop_keepout parameter; cec_synth_pipeline elicit_requirements respect_antenna_keepout
source: CLAUDE.md done-items EPS re-condensed: 'ESP32-C6 antenna keepout DROPPED (no wireless, per user) -> GND fills under it, courtyard trimmed to body'

title: LP5907 LDO input and output bypass caps must be within 2 mm of LDO pins
rule: The LP5907 LDO (U3 or equivalent) input bypass cap (10 uF, C_in) and output bypass cap (1 uF, C_out) must each be placed within 2 mm of their respective LDO pins. The LP5907 has no BYP pin (pin 4 = NC); bypass is only on IN and OUT.
scope: All boards with LP5907. Refs: U3 (LP5907), C_in (10 uF on IN net), C_out (1 uF on OUT/+3V3 net).
rationale: LDO stability requires low-ESR capacitance close to the IN and OUT pins to maintain phase margin. A long trace between LDO and bypass cap adds inductance, risking oscillation under load transients.
check_method: Find LP5907 IN and OUT pads. Find caps on the same nets within the cluster. Fail if distance > 2 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items: 'LP5907 LDO (SNVS798Q)... pin4=NC, no BYP'; vendored symbol pinout audit

title: CAN_H and CAN_L must route as a coupled differential pair, length-matched
rule: CAN_H and CAN_L traces must be routed as a coupled pair (CAN netclass, 0.25 mm width, consistent spacing). They must run in parallel for their entire length, with spacing <= 0.3 mm between the two. Length mismatch between CAN_H and CAN_L traces must be <= 2 mm.
scope: All boards. Nets /CAN_H and /CAN_L.
rationale: CAN is a differential bus. Equal-length, tightly-spaced traces reduce common-mode noise pickup and ensure matched propagation delay. For 500 kbps (and optional 1 Mbps) CAN, differential routing is the baseline SI requirement.
check_method: Identify CAN_H and CAN_L tracks. Compare total lengths; fail if |L_H - L_L| > 2 mm. Check average spacing between parallel segments; warn if > 0.5 mm.
existing_checker: cec_score.diffpair_ok (gates on routing completeness, not spacing/length)
source: CLAUDE.md netclasses: 'CAN 0.25 coupled /CAN_H,/CAN_L'; spec §3.1: 'Classical CAN at 500 kbps'

title: USB D+/D- must be routed as a matched differential pair with exactly 1 via for layer swap
rule: USB_D_P and USB_D_N must be routed as a differential pair (USB netclass, 0.25 mm width, 0.13 mm gap). Length mismatch must be <= 0.5 mm. Exactly one via is permitted per trace for the D+/D- side-swap (U1 to J5 layer crossover), not more.
scope: All boards with USB-C J5. Nets /USB_D_P and /USB_D_N.
rationale: USB Full Speed (12 Mbps) requires a differential pair with controlled impedance (90 ohm differential). Length mismatch causes phase skew that increases common-mode noise. A via introduces impedance discontinuity; more than one per trace amplifies this.
check_method: Count vias on each USB net; fail if > 1. Compute length mismatch; fail if > 0.5 mm. Check pair spacing for the diff-pair sections.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items EPS routing: 'routed the USB diff pair (with a D+/D- via-swap for the J5<->U1 side crossover)'; netclasses: 'USB 0.25 diff gap0.13 /USB_D_P,/USB_D_N'

title: At least 5 mm separation between shunt resistors and precision sense ICs
rule: No precision voltage/current sense IC (INA228, INA238, INA240, INA181, REF3030, LP5907) should have its centroid within 5 mm of any shunt resistor centroid, except for the INA directly paired with that shunt (Kelvin adjacent pair). The paired INA-to-shunt proximity is required (see sense-ic-adjacent-shunt-kelvin constraint); other precision ICs must be separated.
scope: All boards. Shunts RS*. Precision ICs: all INA*, REF*, LP5907 refs.
rationale: Shunts dissipate I^2*R heat under load. On 12VHPWR at 6.7A/shunt with 1 mOhm = 45 mW/shunt x6 = 270 mW total shunt heating. A reference or LDO adjacent to a shunt will have elevated temperature, causing offset errors. The 5 mm separation (filled with GND copper or air gap) provides adequate thermal isolation.
check_method: For each (shunt RS*, precision IC) pair that are NOT the primary Kelvin pair, compute centroid distance. Fail if < 5 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md action item -2: '(3) the rest of the considerations list (thermal sep, routing channels, diff-pair proximity, symmetry) as hard constraints/score terms'; spec §6.6: 'chassis thermal coupling / TIM under the EPS/PCIe shunts'

title: EPS/PCIe shunts require a bare copper TIM land for chassis thermal coupling
rule: Each shunt resistor on EPS and PCIe boards must have a bare-copper (solder-mask-open) contact land on the bottom of the board directly under the shunt body, for chassis thermal coupling via TIM (thermal interface material). The mask-open area must be >= the shunt body footprint area.
scope: EPS/PCIe boards only. Each RS* shunt.
rationale: EPS/PCIe shunts carry 40-55A per cable (OQ-10). At 0.5 mOhm and 40A, each shunt dissipates 0.8W. Without chassis coupling the shunts self-heat well above ambient, degrading measurement accuracy and potentially damaging the PCB. TIM + bare copper land allows heat to flow into the chassis/heatsink.
check_method: For each RS* shunt, check if the footprint includes a mask-open (solder mask opening) on B.Cu under the shunt body. Flag if absent.
source: spec §6.6 (CLAUDE.md v3.8): 'chassis thermal coupling (a TIM pad and bare contact land under the EPS/PCIe shunts, Section 6.6)'; CLAUDE.md action item -2 considerations

title: INA181 and TLV7011 detection front-end must be in the cable column, INA181 rot 180
rule: On EPS and PCIe boards, each cable's INA181 (gain-50 CSA) and TLV7011 (hysteresis comparator) must be placed in the same cable column as their associated shunt, between J_IN and J_OUT vertically. INA181 must be at rot 180 so its IN+/IN- (HI/LO sense pads, pins 3/4) face the shunt.
scope: EPS/PCIe boards with §6.13 detection front-end. U20-22 (INA181), U30-32 (TLV7011) per cable.
rationale: The §6.13 detection front-end connects to the same SENSE_HI/LO nodes as the INA238, so it must be in the same column for short Kelvin-tap access. INA181 at rot 180 aligns the IN+/IN- pads toward the shunt inner edge, mirroring the INA238 placement convention.
check_method: For each cable column c: verify INA181 X-centroid is within ±2 mm of shunt RS_c X-centroid. Verify INA181 rotation = 180 (or equivalent mod 360).
source: gen-eps-condensed.py: 'P[f"U2{i}"] = (Xc + 11.8, 15.0, 180)'; CLAUDE.md done-items: 'INA181 rot 0->180'

title: Shunt RS* must be at rot 270 so pad 1 (_HI) is the upper terminal facing J_IN
rule: All shunt resistors on EPS/PCIe boards must be placed at rotation 270 degrees. At rot 270: pad 1 is the upper terminal (connected to _HI net, facing J_IN / PSU side), pad 2 is the lower terminal (connected to _LO net, facing J_OUT / load side). A rot 90 orientation would invert HI and LO, causing Kelvin tap crossings.
scope: EPS/PCIe boards. All RS* shunt refs (R_2512 footprint).
rationale: The Kelvin sense convention is HI = PSU-side, LO = load-side. At rot 270, pad 1 (HI) is on top and pad 2 (LO) is on bottom, so sense traces exit the shunt inner edges without crossing. At rot 90, pad 1 would be at the bottom, requiring the HI trace to cross the LO trace to reach the INA IN+ pin.
check_method: For each RS* ref, check footprint rotation value. Fail if rotation is not 270 (mod 360).
source: gen-eps-condensed.py: 'P[f"RS{c}"] = (Xc + 6.8, 17.5, 270)'; CLAUDE.md done-items: 'shunt rot 90->270 so HI is the upper terminal -> Kelvin no longer crosses'

title: 12V high-current traces must meet IPC-2221 thermal limits; prefer pours
rule: Any copper carrying 12V rail current (nets matching /SENSEC*_HI or +12V) must either: (a) be a filled copper zone/pour of >= 1.5 mm^2 cross-section per ampere (at dT=20°C, 2oz copper), or (b) a trace of at least 2.5 mm width for single-layer or IPC-2221 equivalently. The preferred form is additive pours after routing (cec_fr.add_power_pours), not fat traces.
scope: EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR boards. Nets: SENSEC*_HI (cable HI = full cable current), +12V pours in J3/J4 pin columns on 12VHPWR.
rationale: EPS/PCIe carry 40-55A per cable. 12VHPWR carries ~6.7A per pin lane. IPC-2221 requires copper cross-section scaled to current. Freerouting ignores netclass widths and routes at 0.2mm default — a 12V net at 0.2mm is a fab disaster. The correct architecture is pours, not fat traces.
check_method: For each track segment on a 12V net: compute cross-section = width_mm * copper_thickness_mm (0.07mm for 1oz, 0.14mm for 2oz). Fail if cross-section < current_A / 1.5. Flag any 12V track segment < 1.5 mm width.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items routing: 'MAJOR REVIEW FINDING -- TRACE SIZING IS NOT HONOURED: Freerouting IGNORES the netclass widths... A 12V net at 0.2mm is a fab disaster'; cec_fr.add_power_pours

title: 24-pin module J1 RJ-45 pin 1 (VCC) must be NC, not tied to +5VSB
rule: On the 24-pin ATX module, the RJ-45 connector J1 pin 1 (VCC / +5VSB) must be left as NO-CONNECT in the netlist. It must NOT be connected to the +5VSB net or any power rail. (Other modules' J1 pin 1 VCC stays connected to +5VSB — this rule is unique to the 24-pin module.)
scope: 24-pin ATX module ONLY. J1.1 net.
rationale: The 24-pin module is both the bulk 5VSB source (via dedicated JST feed to the Hub) and a module on a port. If J1.1 is tied to +5VSB, it creates a parallel path from the 5VSB rail through the RJ-45 VCC pin (1.5A rated contact) directly to the Hub's power rail, bypassing the TPS2121 mux and potentially carrying bulk current through an undersized contact.
check_method: From netlist: verify J1 pin 1 has no net connection (NC) on the 24-pin ATX module. Fail if it is connected to +5VSB or any power net.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions: '24-pin RJ-45 VCC is NO-CONNECT (LOCKED, spec §2.7 v3.3): the 24-pin module is both the bulk 5VSB source... its own RJ-45 VCC pin (J1.1) is left open — NOT tied to its +5VSB'

title: DETECT R1 must match the §2.3 code table for the module type
rule: The DETECT ID resistor (R1, pin 8 of RJ-45 to GND) must be the exact value from the §2.3 code table: CAN-only modules (24-pin, EPS, PCIe, 12VHPWR Standard) = 2.2 kOhm; 12VHPWR Pro = 4.7 kOhm; CAN+100BASE-T1 modules = 10 kOhm. No other values are valid.
scope: All modules. R1 net: pin 8 of J1 (RJ-45) to GND.
rationale: The DETECT code table is locked (OQ-6 resolved v1.7). The Hub reads the divider voltage to determine link class. An incorrect R1 value causes the Hub to either miss the module entirely (wrong voltage band) or bring up the wrong link type.
check_method: Read R1 BOM value. For 24-pin/EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR-Std: fail if value != 2200 ohm (2.2k). For 12VHPWR Pro: fail if value != 4700 ohm.
source: spec §2.3; CLAUDE.md: 'DETECT code table RESOLVED v1.7 (OQ-6), encoding LINK CAPABILITY: CAN-only 2.2 kΩ (0.595 V), CAN+RS-485 4.7 kΩ (1.055 V)'

title: Shunt values must match §6.4 table per module
rule: Shunt resistor values must exactly match spec §6.4: 24-pin ATX 12V/5V/3V3 rails = 2 mOhm, 24-pin 5VSB = 25 mOhm; EPS per-cable = 0.5 mOhm; PCIe per-cable = 0.5 mOhm; 12VHPWR per-pin = 1 mOhm.
scope: All modules. All RS* shunt refs.
rationale: Shunt values are sized for the full-scale current of each rail, calibrated for 0.1-1% accuracy at rated current. An incorrect value shifts the current measurement full-scale range and may cause INA input saturation (too small) or resolution loss (too large).
check_method: From BOM: for each RS* ref, read value. Cross-check against spec §6.4 table by board name. Fail on any mismatch.
source: spec §6.4; CLAUDE.md: 'Shunt values (spec §6.4, LOCKED; parts pending OQ-11): 24-pin 12V/5V/3V3 = 2 mΩ, 24-pin 5VSB = 25 mΩ; EPS and PCIe per-cable = 0.5 mΩ; 12VHPWR per-pin = 1 mΩ'

title: Vias on 12V high-current paths must be 0.5 mm drill / 0.9 mm pad, clustered 5-6 per shunt terminal
rule: Any via connecting F.Cu to B.Cu on a 12V high-current net (SENSEC*_HI or equivalent) must use 0.5 mm drill / 0.9 mm pad size. Multiple vias must be used per shunt terminal: at least 5-6 vias per shunt pad and 3-6 per J3/J4 power pin. A single via on a 40A cable path is a fusing risk.
scope: EPS/PCIe boards. All vias on SENSEC*_HI nets. 12VHPWR: all vias on +12V lane nets.
rationale: A single 0.5mm drill via carries approximately 2A at dT=10°C. 40A per cable requires a minimum of 20 vias; 5-6 per shunt terminal spread across both shunt pads is the minimum for acceptable current density. Under-viaed high-current transitions are a thermal fusing hazard.
check_method: For each high-current net, count vias in the pcbnew model. Fail if total via count < current_A / 2 (IPC estimate per via at 10°C rise). Additionally flag any individual via with drill < 0.5 mm on a 12V net.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline electrothermal_solve (via current split + barrel cross-section)
source: CLAUDE.md done-items 12VHPWR routing plan: 'current-carrying vias 0.5mm drill / 0.9mm pad (~2A @10C), stitch F<->B ~5mm down each lane + a field of 5-6 per shunt terminal + 3-6 per J3/J4 power pin'

title: Three fiducial markers must be placed, non-collinear, at known positions
rule: Every board must have exactly 3 fiducial markers (cec-Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm, board_only / excl-BOM / excl-pos) placed at board corners or mid-edges, non-collinear (not all on the same X or Y line). Fiducials must be labeled FID1, FID2, FID3.
scope: All boards. FID1, FID2, FID3.
rationale: Pick-and-place machines require at least 3 non-collinear fiducials for board registration during assembly. Two fiducials allow only 2D translation correction; a third adds rotation. JLCPCB requires fiducials for SMD assembly.
check_method: Count FID* refs. Fail if != 3. Check non-collinearity: fail if all three share the same X or Y coordinate within 0.5 mm.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items: 'fiducials DONE 2026-06-06 (3x cec-Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm, board_only/excl-BOM/excl-pos, refs on F.Fab: FID1 (162.25,61) TR, FID2 (166,135.5) BR, FID3 (139,116) lower-center; DRC copper-clean)'

title: RJ-45 FTP jack shield tabs SH1 and SH2 must both connect to GND
rule: On all boards using the cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal footprint (Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C / LCSC C2683360), both SH1 and SH2 shield tab pads must be connected to the GND net. Neither tab may be NC or floating.
scope: Hub Standard J2-J5; EPS J1; 12VHPWR-Std J1; and any board emitted by gen-modules.py after FTP migration.
rationale: Both-end shielding + grounding (SH1 and SH2 both to GND) is the platform standard for chassis-bonded RJ-45 modules on short cables. A floating shield provides no EMI benefit and can become an antenna.
check_method: For each RJ-45 instance using the FTP footprint, verify SH1 and SH2 pad nets = GND in the netlist.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'Shield SH1/SH2 TIED TO GND (both ends shielded AND grounded, per user)'; FTP migration note: 'gen-modules.py now EMITS the FTP footprint + SH1/SH2->GND'

title: 4700 uF hold-up cap must be on isolated +5V_HOLD reservoir, after the D1 Schottky
rule: The 4700 uF aluminum electrolytic (Panasonic EEVFK1C472M) must be placed on the +5V_HOLD net (the isolated reservoir side of D1 Schottky), NOT directly on +5VSB. The net sequence must be: +5VSB_RAW -> TPS2121 mux -> (D1 cathode = +5V_HOLD node) -> 4700 uF to GND -> LP5907 LDO IN.
scope: Hub Standard board only. C1 (4700 uF), D1 (SB120 or SS14 Schottky), net +5V_HOLD.
rationale: D1 isolates the reservoir from the +5VSB rail during fast power interruptions, so the hold-up cap maintains power to the MCU during a brief outage. If C1 were on +5VSB directly, D1 would be backwards (blocking discharge) or pointless. Per OQ-56: bench-verify 4700uF rides a flash write.
check_method: Trace the net of C1 positive terminal. Must be +5V_HOLD (or equivalent isolated reservoir net), NOT +5VSB or +5VSB_RAW. Verify D1 cathode is on the same net as C1+.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'D1 is the downstream Schottky isolating the +5V_HOLD reservoir — BUILT as SB120 (1A/20V)'; CLAUDE.md action items: '4700 uF aluminum electrolytic hold-up — Panasonic EEVFK1C472M 16 V, corrected from polymer v1.9'

title: INA240 must be the SOIC-8 D-package (INA240A3DR), never the TSSOP/PW package
rule: All INA240 instances must use the D-package (SOIC-8, 1.27mm pitch, 8 pads, MPN INA240A3DR, LCSC C2060584). The PW package (TSSOP-8) has a DIFFERENT pin numbering and is electrically incompatible with the D-package schematic symbol. Never substitute PW.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. All INA240 refs.
rationale: The D (SOIC-8) and PW (TSSOP-8) packages of the INA240 have different pin assignments. Placing a PW part on a D-package footprint connects the wrong pins to the wrong signals, creating a dangerous inversion of the sense amplifier. This is not a silent failure — it will produce incorrect current readings.
check_method: For each INA240 ref, verify BOM MPN ends in 'DR' (SOIC-8 D-package). Fail if MPN ends in 'PW' or footprint is TSSOP.
source: CLAUDE.md vendored symbol audit: 'the orderable MPN MUST be the D part (INA240A3DR), never the PW — the symbol value is currently package-ambiguous INA240A3 (pin the D suffix + LCSC# at the 12VHPWR BOM pass)'

title: DETECT ESD diode must be PESD5V0S1BA (SOD-323), never PESD5V0S1UL (SOD-882/DFN1006)
rule: All DETECT pin-8 ESD diodes must use PESD5V0S1BA in SOD-323 footprint (LCSC C5261083). The PESD5V0S1UL part is only available from JLCPCB/LCSC in DFN1006/SOD-882 package — not SOD-323. Using UL on a BA (SOD-323) land creates an unsoldered or incorrect footprint.
scope: All boards. D2-D5 (Hub Standard), D1 (all modules).
rationale: SOD-323 and SOD-882/DFN1006 are different package sizes and pad geometries. The BA suffix = SOD-323 (the board land); the UL suffix = SOD-882/DFN1006 (wrong physical size). Ordering the UL part for a BA land results in misaligned pads and likely opens or partial connections.
check_method: For each ESD diode ref (D2-D5 on Hub, D1 on modules): verify BOM Value = 'PESD5V0S1BA' and LCSC = C5261083. Fail if Value = 'PESD5V0S1UL' or LCSC = C2011513.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'part corrected from PESD5V0S1UL to the SOD-323 sibling PESD5V0S1BA on 2026-06-05 — the UL is only stocked in DFN1006/SOD-882 by LCSC, the BA is the SOD-323 part'

title: Cable column pitch must be uniform and >= 20 mm on EPS/PCIe boards
rule: On EPS/PCIe boards, the center-to-center X distance between adjacent cable columns (each column = J_IN_n + shunt RS_n + INA238_n + J_OUT_n) must be equal for all adjacent pairs and >= 20 mm (PCIe-3port minimum at 20 mm pitch). EPS and PCIe-2port use 23 mm pitch. Deviation between adjacent columns must be <= 0.5 mm.
scope: EPS/PCIe boards. Cable column X positions derived from J_IN_n or shunt RS_n X-centroids.
rationale: Uniform pitch ensures equal-length 12V force traces and equal shunt heating distribution. Non-uniform pitch means some columns have longer traces with higher resistance, biasing the current distribution. It also complicates pour routing.
check_method: Extract X-positions of RS_n shunts, sort by cable index. Compute adjacent differences. Fail if max(diff) - min(diff) > 0.5 mm. Fail if any pitch < 20 mm.
source: gen-eps-condensed.py: 'CX0, PITCH, H = 11.0, 23.0, 37.0'; gen-pcie-condensed (CLAUDE.md): '2-port 86.4x44 (pitch 23), 3-port 103.4x44 (pitch 20)'

title: Rail divider R5/R6 on 12VHPWR Standard must be 0.1% tolerance resistors
rule: R5 (47k) and R6 (10k) on the 12VHPWR Standard rail voltage divider must be sourced at 0.1% tolerance, 25 ppm/°C or better. Yageo RT0402BRD0747KL (C728561) for R5, RT0402BRD0710KL (C190095) for R6. Standard 1% resistors are not acceptable for this divider.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board only. R5 (47k, VRAIL_DIV input) and R6 (10k, VRAIL_DIV to GND).
rationale: The REF3030 ratiometric reference cancels ADC gain/offset drift but NOT the divider-ratio error. A 1% resistor pair can have 2% total ratio error, limiting voltage accuracy to ~2%. The 0.1% pair limits ratio error to ~0.2%, enabling the ~0.3-0.5% voltage channel accuracy specified.
check_method: Read R5 and R6 BOM Tolerance field. Fail if Tolerance > 0.1%. Or: verify LCSC for R5 = C728561 and R6 = C190095.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'the REF3030 ratiometric ref does NOT cancel divider-ratio error, so 0.1% is required... Repointed R5 -> Yageo RT0402BRD0747KL (C728561, 47k 0.1% 25ppm) and R6 -> RT0402BRD0710KL (C190095, 10k 0.1% 25ppm)'

title: INA240 input filter resistors RFH/RFL (12 total) must be 0.1% tolerance
rule: All 12 INA240 input filter resistors (RFH1-6 and RFL1-6, each 10 ohm) on the 12VHPWR Standard board must be 0.1% tolerance, 50 ppm/°C or better. Yageo RT0402BRE0710RL (C705642). Standard 1% resistors degrade CMRR.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board. RFH1-6, RFL1-6 (all 10 ohm, R_0402).
rationale: The RC anti-alias filter uses matched 10-ohm resistors on IN+ and IN- of each INA240. A mismatch between RFH and RFL creates a differential imbalance that degrades CMRR, allowing common-mode 12V switching noise to appear as a differential measurement error. 0.1% matching keeps the CMRR degradation negligible.
check_method: Read BOM Tolerance for all RFH*/RFL* refs. Fail if any Tolerance > 0.1%.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'RFH/RFL filter 10ohm DONE 2026-06-06 -> 0.1% Yageo RT0402BRE0710RL (C705642, 0.1%/50ppm) on all 12 for AC CMRR on the transient capture'

title: 24-pin ATX module J3/J4 must be Molex 5569 MALE 24-circuit headers, not female
rule: The 24-pin ATX module J3 (PSU-side input) and J4 (motherboard-side output) must both be Molex 5569 MALE right-angle 24-circuit headers. Female receptacles must not be used on the board.
scope: 24-pin ATX module only. J3 and J4.
rationale: No board-mount FEMALE 24-pin ATX receptacle exists as a standard part. Both J3 and J4 are male headers: the PSU's female cable plugs onto J3; a dedicated female-to-female bridging cable connects J4 to the motherboard male header. The convention is board=male, inserting cable end=female.
check_method: Verify J3 and J4 BOM description contains 'Male' or footprint indicates male header orientation. Fail if description contains 'Female' or receptacle.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions §2.8: 'Both J3 and J4 are the Molex 5569 right-angle male footprint — do not fix one to female'

title: Hub Standard J7 (NanoKVM aux) must use S5B-PH-K-S right-angle JST-PH, not top-entry
rule: J7 on Hub Standard must use the right-angle S5B-PH-K-S (LCSC C157923, footprint JST_PH_S5B-PH-K-S_1x05_P2.00mm_Horizontal). The top-entry B5B-PH-K-S (C157993) is explicitly forbidden. The cable must exit parallel to the board (side-entry).
scope: Hub Standard board only. J7.
rationale: A cased Hub does not have vertical headroom for a top-entry JST-PH connector. The right-angle form routes the NanoKVM cable parallel to the board and out a board edge, fitting within the case envelope. This is locked per spec v3.9/v3.7 (OQ-51).
check_method: Verify J7 BOM Value = 'S5B-PH-K-S' and LCSC = C157923. Fail if BOM contains 'B5B-PH-K-S' or LCSC = C157993.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'J7 NanoKVM aux header... 5-pin RIGHT-ANGLE JST-PH S5B-PH-K-S (J7, LCSC C157923)... changed from top-entry B5B-PH-K-S/C157993 per the v3.9 right-angle correction'

title: 12VHPWR 4 sideband sense pins must pass through AND tap to ESP32 GPIO via 1k series R
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard board, all four sideband pins (SENSE0/J3.13, SENSE1/J3.14, CARD_PWR_STABLE/J3.15, CARD_CBL_PRES#/J3.16) must: (1) pass through from J3 to J4 in the netlist, AND (2) each tap a free ESP32-S3 GPIO (IO8, IO9, IO11, IO12 respectively) via a 1k series resistor (R10-R13). The R10-R13 resistors must be placed adjacent to J3 sideband pads.
scope: 12VHPWR Standard board only. Sideband nets, R10-R13, ESP32 IO8/9/11/12.
rationale: The 12V-2x6 sideband pins encode the cable's advertised power capability (SENSE0/1) and present/stable state (CARD_PWR_STABLE, CARD_CBL_PRES#). The module must both pass these signals through to the GPU and report them over CAN. The 1k series resistor protects the ESP32 GPIO from ESD and voltage spikes.
check_method: From netlist: verify each sideband net connects to both J3 and J4 pins AND an ESP32 GPIO via a 1k series resistor. Fail if any sideband net is only connected to J3/J4 but not to the MCU, or vice versa.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.4: '(b) The four 12V-2x6 sideband sense pins (13-16: SENSE0, SENSE1, CARD_PWR_STABLE, CARD_CBL_PRES#) now pass through J3->J4 AND each taps a free ESP32-S3 GPIO (IO8/9/11/12) via a 1k series R (R10-R13)'

title: Standard-tier modules must leave RS-485 pair (pins 4/5) unused and terminated at the module side
rule: On all Standard-tier modules (24-pin, EPS, PCIe, 12VHPWR Standard), RJ-45 pins 4 (STREAM_P) and 5 (STREAM_N) must have no active RS-485 driver or receiver connected. The RS-485 pair should be terminated at the module side (not driven, passively terminated or left open).
scope: All Standard-tier modules. Pins 4 and 5 of J1 (RJ-45).
rationale: RS-485 streaming is a Pro+ feature. Standard modules have no RS-485 transceiver. Connecting pins 4/5 to a driver on a Standard module would inject signals onto a line the Standard Hub has no receiver for, potentially causing bus conflicts if multiple modules share a cable run.
check_method: From netlist: verify J1 pin 4 and pin 5 on Standard modules are either NC or connected only to a termination resistor. Fail if connected to a transceiver TX/RX pin.
source: CLAUDE.md pin allocation table: 'Standard tier leaves pair 2 unused, terminated at the module side'; spec §2.2

title: RJ-45 pin 7 must be a reserved spare, NOT connected to any reference or signal
rule: RJ-45 pin 7 (T568B white-brown, pair 4 mate) must be NC (no-connect) in the netlist of every board. It must not be connected to a precision reference voltage (AUX_REF, REF3033 output, etc.), CAN, RS-485, or any active signal. It is a reserved spare.
scope: All boards. J1 pin 7 (and J2-J5 pin 7 on Hub Standard).
rationale: Pin 7 was formerly considered for a distributed reference (AUX_REF) in earlier spec revisions (OQ-3 pre-resolution). That use was explicitly rejected in spec v1.1 / OQ-3 resolved. Any board that still connects pin 7 to a reference is implementing a stale design.
check_method: From netlist: verify J1 pin 7 has no net connection (NC) on every board. Fail if connected to AUX_REF, REF3033, or any non-GND, non-NC signal.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'pin 7 is a reserved spare, NOT AUX_REF'; spec §2.2 pin table: 'Reserved spare (no distributed reference; see Section 3.3)'

title: 120-ohm CAN split termination must be at the Hub, not on any module
rule: The 120-ohm CAN bus termination (implemented as 60+60 ohm split resistors + 4.7 nF Y-cap) must be present at the Hub and absent from all modules. No module may have a CAN termination resistor between CAN_H and CAN_L or between CAN_H/CAN_L and GND (other than the transceiver's own bus-pin protection).
scope: Hub Standard/Pro: R_term_H and R_term_L (60 ohm each) + Y-cap. All modules: no termination.
rationale: CAN is a terminated bus. The termination must be at the bus ends (the Hub is one end). A module adding termination mid-bus would create a double-terminated (or multi-terminated) stub, reflecting signals and causing CAN errors.
check_method: From netlist: on Hub, verify a resistor pair (each 55-65 ohm) between CAN_H/CAN_L and a common node + Y-cap to GND. On each module, verify no resistor between CAN_H and CAN_L (and no resistor to GND on either net except through the TJA1051T/3 bus-pin protection).
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'Termination: fixed 120 ohm split at Hub'; CLAUDE.md: 'no CAN termination (Hub-only)'

title: 4700 uF electrolytic hold-up cap must be oriented with positive terminal on +5V_HOLD net
rule: C1 (4700 uF aluminum electrolytic, Panasonic EEVFK1C472M 16V) must be placed with its positive terminal on the +5V_HOLD net (~5V) and negative terminal on GND. The footprint must have a visible polarity indicator (stripe on the negative side) that aligns with GND.
scope: Hub Standard board only. C1.
rationale: An aluminum electrolytic capacitor reverse-biased beyond its reverse voltage rating (typically 1-2V for a 16V part) will be damaged or fail catastrophically. At 5V the cap is fine in the correct orientation; reversed it would see -5V and fail shortly after power-up.
check_method: Verify C1 positive pad net = +5V_HOLD. Verify C1 negative pad net = GND. Check footprint polarity marker alignment in the render.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'BUILT as SB120 (1A/20V)... 4700 uF aluminum electrolytic hold-up — Panasonic EEVFK1C472M 16 V'

title: CEC copper logo on B.Cu must not be placed under the ESP32 module footprint
rule: The CEC copper logo footprint on B.Cu must not overlap with the ESP32 module courtyard or body silhouette. The logo must be placed outside the ESP32 courtyard bounding box.
scope: All boards with ESP32 module. Logo footprint on B.Cu.
rationale: A copper logo under the ESP32 module creates unwanted copper fills on B.Cu that may interfere with the module's ground plane, ESP32 test pads, and flash/PSRAM traces. On the EPS board this was explicitly identified as a bug that blocked B.Cu escape routing.
check_method: Find logo footprint centroid. Find ESP32 courtyard bounding box. Fail if logo centroid is inside the ESP32 courtyard bounding box.
source: CLAUDE.md done-items EPS routing: 'move the B.Cu CEC LOGO off the ESP underside (it blocks the natural B.Cu escape)'

title: Module-to-Hub link connector must be RJ-45, never Mini-Fit Jr
rule: The module-to-Hub interface connector (J1 on modules, J2-J5 on Hub Standard) must be RJ-45 8P8C. No Molex Mini-Fit Jr connector may be used for this link. Exception: the 24-pin ATX module's PSU-side power path J3/J4 are Molex Mini-Fit Jr BY DESIGN — this is correct.
scope: All boards. J1 on modules; J2-J5 on Hub Standard.
rationale: Mini-Fit Jr is retired as the module-to-Hub interconnect platform-wide (spec v1.x Mini-Fit Jr re-cut complete). RJ-45 is the locked connector for the universal interface.
check_method: For each hub-interface connector footprint, verify it matches cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal or equivalent RJ-45 footprint. Fail if footprint contains 'Mini-Fit' or 'MFJ' or '5569' or '45586'.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions: 'Module-to-Hub connector is RJ-45 (8P8C) for all tiers, all modules, all Hubs. Mini-Fit Jr is retired as the module-to-Hub interconnect'
